transcript: is this just another recession indicator on Broadway or no? what is the deal  with “It’s a Wonderful Life: a Live Radio Play” coming to Broadway this was just announced with a very interesting cast we got Lisa Rinna in there making her Broadway debut I believe got Titus Burgess as Clarence and of course it's led by Andrew Rannells as George Bailey but what is a live radio play? is this just a fancier way of branding yet another show where actors read from a script into a microphone? not exactly, at least from what I can tell. this live radio play version of It’s a Wonderful Life has actually existed for decades it was adapted by Joe Landry and seems to have a bit more of a fully realized framing device set in a 1940s radio studio where they perform It’s a Wonderful Life as an old timey radio play. there's live foley effects, Carol singing, I've never seen it but it's been performed at regional theaters across the country for the past like 30 years it seems to be pretty popular having said that your gut instinct to call it a recession indicator is probably still not far off base it's probably pretty cheap to throw up on short notice to fill this empty slot in the season at the Broadhurst and I would guess that the actors are gonna be reading from scripts to some extent. so in those two regards it might not be that unlike All In, Celebrity Autobiography, etc. And yes it seems highly likely that we're seeing an influx of these productions because costs are getting so crazy and because these theaters were otherwise sitting empty during these periods of time. and I know the big controversy with these types of shows is that they're still charging Broadway level prices and I'm of two minds on this as I've said before I think it's a bit of a false equivalency to compare this to other Broadway shows like theoretically an event can be valuable for a number of different reasons And as I've said before I do think reading from a script is not the most heinous crime against humanity in the world the way people talk about it if it's built into the format of the show but I also appreciate what someone said to me (I can't remember who; if it was you feel free to take credit in the comments) That even if the format is artistically valid it might just be better suited for 92nd Street Y or SymphonySpace or Town Hall rather than Broadway. regardless of where you land on that in this case at least, the title tells you what it is you have been warned. there is also information out there about past productions if you wanna do further research so everyone can stay calm and make your ticket buying decisions accordingly
